title: A relativistic ring beam in a drift tube as a body of revolution: its space-charge depression
source: A thin annular electron beam of radius r_b in a grounded pipe of radius R, held on its lines by a strong axial magnetic field and injected at γ₀ through a grounded plane, slows to γ_b with I = I₀(γ₀ − γ_b)β_b/(2 ln(R/r_b)), I₀ = 4πε₀mc³/e = 17.045 kA (L. S. Bogdankevich, A. A. Rukhadze, Sov. Phys. Usp. 14:163, 1971; R. B. Miller, An Introduction to the Physics of Intense Charged Particle Beams, Plenum 1982, §3.2). γ₀ = 3 (1.022 MeV), R = 10 mm, r_b = 6 mm: I_L = I₀(γ₀^{2/3} − 1)^{3/2}/(2 ln(R/r_b)) = 18.728 kA; at 0.7 of it, 13.109 kA, γ_b = 2.10734 (the faster root, by bisection). Evaluated apart from the code under test (CODATA 2018 constants)

quantities.quantity: the beam's γ in the middle third of the tube at 13.109 kA, a body of revolution on cells 8 times finer along z
quantities.reason: the depression γ₀ − γ_b to 0.4 % here (1.2 % allowed): the ring half a cell thick (5.75 to 6.25 mm on 1 mm cells) and the tube's ends; on square cells the Yee grid's numerical Cherenkov instability deepens it by a fifth (emcraft_fdtd::axi)

quantities.quantity: the current reaching the far end (A; electrons arriving: negative)
quantities.reason: below the limiting current all of it passes, over the run's second half
